story: The income tax department has not given me my refund of Rs 23,400 for last year's return. It has been 8 months. How do I get my refund?

timeline.event: 8 months have passed since filing last year's tax return

facts.user_goal: Get the income tax refund of Rs 23,400

rules.name: government_party
rules.message: The other side is a government body. If you ever need to file a civil suit in court against the Government or a public officer, the law first requires a written notice and a two-month wait. This rule is about court suits; ask free legal aid (15100) whether it affects your route.
rules.label: Government on the other side

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: I can't work out the time limit for your consumer complaint without the date it started. Please add the date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 23,400, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You are asking about a refund from the Income Tax Department. This is not a consumer dispute. The Consumer Protection Act does not apply to government tax refunds. You need to follow the correct government process or ask free legal aid.

claims.text: The Consumer Protection Act does not apply to getting an income tax refund from the government.
If you need to file a court suit against the Government, the law first requires a written notice and a two-month wait.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to ask how to track your income tax refund.
next_steps.why: They can guide you on the correct government process.

next_steps.action: Call 15100 for free legal aid to ask about your specific income tax refund issue.
next_steps.why: The law says to ask free legal aid if you need to file a court suit against the Government.

questions_for_user: What was the exact date you filed your last year's tax return?
Have you already checked the Income Tax Department's refund status on their website?
not_covered: The specific time limit for a consumer complaint against a government body.
corrections: You cannot file a consumer complaint for an income tax refund. The Consumer Protection Act is for goods and services, not government tax refunds.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: Income Tax Department, [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On [FILL: date of purchase] I paid Rs 23,400 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 23,400 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
escalation_reasons: validator: answer still failed after one retry; failing sentences removed
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, s.80(1) (Two months' notice before a civil SUIT against the Government (not consumer or wage claims)); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
